_note: Competency tiers per assignment (decided 2026-10-20). primary must be MET; secondary (1-2) at least PARTIALLY MET; tertiary never required, noted under ALSO SHOWN when the work shows one. Read by tools/cas-ccps/build-lesson-assignments.js. Every assignment (terms 1-4 and the 8177 lessons placed in no quarter) drafted from each task text and approved as drafted 2026-10-20; tweak entries as lessons are taught. why says which part of the task evidences the primary and secondaries.

8175-L01.why: Part 1 (time period and focus of each of the seven eras, from the Trade Era to the Collaboration Era) evidences explaining marketing as it relates to the industry (39); Part 4 naming the seven functions with two sports/entertainment examples evidences marketing functions (43) and Part 2 contrasting the Selling and Marketing Company eras evidences the marketing concept (41). Revised 2026-10-20: 45 (the industry's past, present and future) was primary, but the task traces marketing's eras, not the industry's history.

8175-L02.why: Naming something the student does out of intrinsic motivation and explaining why they enjoy it evidences personal interests (107); describing what drives them to do it without reward evidences initiative and self-direction (3).

8175-L03.why: Question 2 (the USP and why a team should pick you over 100 other applicants) and Question 3 (who you serve) evidence positioning relative to competitors and as seen by the audience (64); Question 1 (the value your strengths and attributes provide) evidences personal skills (107).

8175-L04.why: Sections 1 and 3 (what makes the figure known, how others describe them) evidence explaining a brand and its personality (56); Section 2 (a strength, weakness, opportunity and threat) evidences SWOT components (105) and judging whether the public reputation matches who they really seem to be evidences critical thinking (2). Opportunity and threat added 2026-10-20.

8175-L05.why: The 5-sentence reflection on current support communities, what they have done for the student and which ones hinder success evidences life-management skills (12); explaining how the student will join new communities that offer support evidences initiative and self-direction (3). Revised 2026-10-20: 109 (an industry networking plan) was secondary, but the task is about personal support, not industry contacts.

8175-L06.why: The 100-word plan to practice soft skills (patience, face-to-face communication, resilience) before a new job evidences professionalism (20); the specific action for an interview setting evidences the interview process (112) and the written plan itself evidences writing (21).

8175-L07.why: The initial post outlining how the student would react to the chosen scenario evidences integrity (4); naming what is unethical in the scenario (favoritism, fudged numbers, derogatory comments, intimidation) evidences ethical vs. unethical practices (51) and the required professional tone of the planned response evidences professionalism (20). Peer replies are not evidence.

8175-L08.why: The 3-5 slide deck following the Rule of Six with a speaker-notes script evidences presentation skills (50); labeling verbal, nonverbal and visual communication in the notes evidences types of communication (48) and the high-contrast slide build in PowerPoint/Google Slides evidences technology proficiency (18).

8175-L09.why: Defining branding (what it is not, the real-brand example, the brand as a promise) evidences explaining branding (56); writing it for someone with no business background evidences translating technical language (54) and the 250-word structured response evidences writing (21).

8175-L10.why: The Action, Emotion and Value questions (what set the company apart, how it felt, what it did to perceived value) evidence the importance of customer service (52); the Recovery question applying the LAST steps evidences complaint-handling procedures (55) and the 10-sentence reflection evidences writing (21).

8175-L11.why: Section 2 assessing the Cavalier brand (logo, colors, reputation) evidences branding in this context (57); Section 1 demographics and psychographics evidences target marketing (42) and the areas for improvement plus Section 3 trends affecting rebranding evidence reasons for rebranding (59).

8175-L12.why: Two internal strengths and weaknesses and two external opportunities and threats evidence SWOT components (105); placing the team against rivals and competitor threats evidences competition in the industry (101).

8175-L13.why: The three open, unbiased focus-group questions (the slide the teacher grades first) evidence the importance of research (103); the 5-7 slide deck evidences presentation skills (50) and the new tagline/theme and desired-future vision evidence creativity (1).

8175-L14.why: The Ownership point (the business's ownership type and how it changes who decides and who takes risk) evidences business ownership (69); the 5-year Future Forecast based on AI and trends evidences trends and innovations (47) and the minimal-text slide deck built from the script evidences presentation skills (50).

8177-the-business-of-the-game.why: Part 3 (top three revenue sources, each with how it brings in money) evidences revenue sources (86); Part 2 (owner and ownership type with how you know) evidences organizational structures (52) and Part 4 (one specific effect on the home city) evidences local economic impact (50).

8177-brand-board.why: Inventing the event or venue and building the brand board (palette, font, two logo versions, three words, four images) evidences creativity (1); Part 4 (how colors and logo show up inside the venue) evidences facilities management/atmospherics (45) and setting the visual identity every campaign for the event will use evidences the manager's decision-making for campaigns (42). Revised 2026-10-20: 93 (what motivates attendance) was secondary; 42 is closer to branding. The 8177 task list has no branding competency.

8177-the-4-ps-of-the-fan-experience.why: Parts 1-5 (product, price, place, promotion and how changing one P affects the others) evidence a marketing plan (97); Part 2 (price, cost to make and profit per item for an item sold only at the venue) evidences on-site revenue streams (46).

8177-chhs-school-store-company-descripti.why: The 5-sentence company description in a professional voice evidences writing (21); naming what the shop is, how it is run, its customers and its USP evidences business-start-up steps (customer segments, value proposition) (56), and writing the company description as the first section of the store's business plan evidences planning within an organization (23). Revised 2026-10-20: 93 (what motivates people to attend events) was secondary; the task is about the store, not an event. The 8177 task list has no branding competency.

8177-what-is-branding-reflection-essay.why: The 500-word essay with a plain definition, three example paragraphs and plain-language term explanations evidences writing (21); Part 1 (what each project taught about branding) and Part 3 (finding and rewriting sentences a beginner wouldn't understand) evidence critical thinking (2).

8177-employee-handbook-operations.why: Part 2's Z-Out (what is counted, the float subtracted, checked against the daily sales report) and Part 3's Two-Person and scan-everything rules against shrink evidence financial responsibility (25); Part 1 (each role's responsibility and what goes wrong without it) evidences personnel needs (95) and Part 4 (what you say to the waiting line) evidences customer-service techniques (58).

8175-L15.why: The 200-word persuasive essay on whether hosting is a smart investment (cost, revenue, white elephants) evidences economic concepts (98); Part 1 research with at least 3 cited sources evidences information literacy (15) and the essay itself evidences writing (21).

8175-L16.why: Part 1 break-even calculations for Scenarios A and B with shown work evidence math (19); choosing and justifying skimming vs. penetration evidences pricing strategies (67) and the priced combo with a fan rationale evidences bundling (95).

8175-L17.why: Identifying producer, intermediary and consumer in the ticket chain evidences distribution (70); the 100-word opinion piece on bot scalping evidences ethical vs. unethical practices (51) and the stadium-vs-club venue question evidences distribution challenges (71).

8175-L18.why: Section 1 (name, concept, rules, appeal of the new sport) evidences product planning (60); Section 2 demographics/psychographics evidences target marketing (42) and Section 3 sponsor selection and rationale evidences sponsorship (87).

8175-L19.why: The two-month hype-cycle timeline and pitch (customer profile, branding message, ad mockup, PR points, metrics) evidence promotional campaign elements (93); the weekly mix of public appearance, fan interaction and interview evidences promotional roles (73) and the cost/payoff estimate evidences ROI analysis (104).

8175-L20.why: The Impact question (how the partnership helps the athlete's personal brand and the non profit) evidences public relations (83); explaining the athlete-cause connection and benefit to both sides evidences big-picture thinking (11), and the cause co-branding partnership evidences a sponsorship trend (90).

8175-L21.why: The 5-sentence naming-rights proposal evidences sponsorship (87); the sponsor-vs-endorser explanation with a reason for each evidences 88, and defining and judging ambush marketing evidences brand protection (58).

8175-L22.why: The Strategy slides (awareness, fundraising idea, chosen promotion) plus visuals evidence a promotional campaign (93); the sales promotion with one advantage and one disadvantage evidences 92, and the original cleat design and three-brand merch item evidence creativity (1).

8175-L23.why: The finished publication (eye-catching cover, articles, layout) evidences creativity (1); the colorful advertisements evidence advertisement elements (75) and 'Going Digital' (two ways to make money online) evidences digital revenue (82).

8177-school-store-planogram-customer-exp.why: The top-down map with traffic flow, bottleneck fix and merchandise/hot/impulse zones evidences facilities management (45); Part 4 marking exits and 36-inch walkways evidences workplace safety (22) and placing each staff member with a reason evidences personnel needs (95).

8177-product-pitch-financial-analysis.why: Part 5 calculations (cost per item, profit, margin, batch cost, break-even, expected profit, turnover) evidence math (19); Part 3 real-supplier materials costing and production capacity evidences financial resources required (96), and Part 2 (who buys it and when) evidences consumer motivation (93).

8177-the-economics-of-the-arena.why: Part 1 revenue calculations at every price for three games evidence math (19); Part 3 explaining why the playoff game outprices Snowy Tuesday evidences popularity/competitive factors and attendance (94), and Parts 2 and 4 (choosing a price from the math, taking a side on fairness) evidence critical thinking (2).

8175-L24.why: Part 1 (define personal and non-personal selling with two benefits and two negatives of each) evidences types of selling (94); Part 2 (the six steps of the selling process in order) evidences the selling process (96).

8175-L25.why: Researching one Black entrepreneur and working three specific, accurate facts about their background and ventures into the card evidences information literacy (15); designing the original Valentine card (format, verse, layout) evidences creativity (1).

8175-L26.why: The Education, Top Strengths, Achievements and Academic Projects categories with two to three specific examples each evidence career planning (12); the Target Organizations and Inspiration categories evidence researching contacts for a networking plan (109).

8175-L27.why: Part 1 (specific marketing examples noticed over break) and the reverse engineering of how the campaign went from idea to ad evidence promotion and the promotional mix (72); Keeping You (follow, email sign-up, loyalty app, discount code) evidences attracting and keeping customers (79) and Was It Worth It (how the company could tell the campaign earned back its cost) evidences ROI (104).

8175-L28.why: Writing two quantitative and one qualitative question meant to find out what customers want from a new service evidences the role of market research (62); the Bias Check (spotting and rewriting leading questions) evidences critical thinking (2) and building and sending the survey in Google Forms evidences IT tools (17).

8175-L29.why: The Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats critique of the class draft survey evidences a SWOT analysis (105); The Fix (specific, actionable changes to the shared class survey) evidences contributing to the team's product (10). Opportunities and threats added 2026-10-20.

8175-L30.why: The 10 closed and 2 open questions designed to verify the class market segments and how to reach them evidence creating a survey for primary research (63); building and sending it in Google Forms evidences IT tools (17).

8175-L31.why: Part 2 (one concrete suggestion for running the league/event differently) evidences critical thinking and decision-making (2); Part 3 (citing the survey data to justify it) evidences using research to build the plan (103) and Protect the Data (no names or emails plus one sentence on why survey data stays private) evidences information security (16).

8175-L32.why: The 200-word essay on predicted workforce changes and how the student will prepare for them, plus naming one job to research further, evidences continuous learning and adaptability (13); researching the five fastest-growing industries and citing three different sources evidences information literacy (15).

8175-L33.why: The one-page resume (header, education, experience with action verbs, soft and hard skills) evidences developing a resume (110); the link to a real posting on TeamWork Online, Indeed, Handshake or a team careers page evidences job-search resources (108).

8175-L34.why: The reflection on what the interview-skills video taught and one specific thing to do in an interview setting evidences the job interview process (112); the 100-word plan to practice those skills before an interview evidences initiative and self-direction (3).

8175-L35.why: The five Interview Warmup questions with polished final answers evidence preparing answers to anticipated interview questions (112); refining each answer from the tool's feedback into a perfected written version evidences being coachable (13).

8175-L36.why: Designing the course brochure with a creative logo and a showcased project evidences creativity (1); Panel Three (three careers the class prepares you for) evidences occupations in the industry (106) and Panel Four (pros and cons of the teaching approach, phrased respectfully) evidences professionalism (20).

8177-market-research-survey-design.why: Part 2 (building the three-question Google Form with email collection off) and Part 3 (whether each question collects quantitative or qualitative data and what the store learns) evidence developing a market research project (83); Part 4 (explaining and rewriting three biased questions) evidences critical thinking (2) and Part 5 (one more primary and one secondary source and what each tells the store) evidences sources of market research data (79).

8177-survey-deployment-statistical-signi.why: The fieldwork itself, Part 1 (why 323 responses instead of a few friends) and Part 4 (the running log of dates, places and response counts) evidence carrying out a market research project (83); Part 3 (when, where and whom to ask beyond close friends) and the log evidence managing time and resources (14), and Part 5 (why every response must be real) with the no-names log evidences integrity (4).

8177-survey-results-analysis.why: Part 1 (three findings stated with their numbers and what each means for the store) evidences evaluating market research results (84); Parts 2-3 (one specific change backed by the numbers) evidence critical thinking (2) and Part 4 (how the results help three marketing functions, or what a future survey should ask) evidences research for all functions of marketing (78).

8177-promotional-flyer-design.why: Designing the black-and-white flyer with a stop-walking headline, logo, hours, location and three real items with prices evidences creativity (1); building it in Canva, Adobe Express or Google Slides with a grayscale logo check and PDF export evidences occupational design tools (18) and Part 2 (explaining hierarchy, contrast and negative space) with the short flyer copy evidences writing (21).

8177-the-hype-machine.why: Parts 1-3 (a paid ad mockup with audience, placement and cost, an earned PR stunt, and a sales promotion with a deadline) evidence a marketing plan for the playoff game (97); Part 4 (allocating the $5,000 item by item) and Part 5 (checking every promise will hold up on game night) evidence the manager's decision-making for a campaign (42).

8177-the-richmond-festival-blueprint.why: Working through all three phases (vision, logistics with a justified Richmond location, business) evidences the event planning process (92); The Team (five specific jobs and what each does) evidences personnel needs (95) and Risk Management (one thing that could go wrong and exactly how to prepare) evidences risk assessment and management (67).

8177-game-day-takeover.why: Part 3 (listing everyone who helped and what they did, a specific thank-you note to one staff member, and a public thank-you to customers) evidences follow-up to recognize and thank participants (99); Part 2's staffing chart (every role, who fills it and who backs them up) evidences personnel needs (95).

8177-tournament-sponsorship-proposal.why: Part 2's one-page formal business letter (hook, connection, value, call to action) proofread in Part 3 evidences writing (21); Part 1 (a real local business, its sponsorship decision-maker and address, and why its customers match the crowd) evidences information literacy (15) and the Value paragraph (exactly what the sponsor gets) evidences sponsorship as part of an event marketing plan (97).

8177-the-millionaire-s-strike.why: Part 1 (each side's position on the four issues), Part 2 (the final deal and what each side gave up) and Part 4 (why owners cannot replace players and why overseas options add leverage) evidence labor issues (28); Part 5 (the NLRA right and why owners want the draft and cap inside a CBA) evidences labor and antitrust law (70) and Part 3 (three local businesses or hourly jobs hurt by a lost season) evidences local economic impact (50).

8177-the-stadium-economy.why: Part 2 (consumer spending and GDP, and which new-spending estimate to trust) and Part 3 (how the interest rate and inflation raise the county's cost, with numbers) evidence economic indicators (49); the verdict comparing yearly loan payments with taxes on truly new spending evidences the stadium's effect on the local economy (50) and Part 4 (a seating capacity justified by diminishing returns) evidences facilities management (45).

8177-the-cloud-behind-the-game.why: Part 3 (how two accurate stories leave opposite impressions through selection, framing, headline, word choice and quotes, plus a balanced rewrite) evidences media bias and public perception (65); Part 2 (the economic, social and environmental T-chart and the AI option) with Part 5 (the evidence-backed recommendation) evidences social and environmental concerns in decisions (64) and Part 4's org chart (at least five roles at launch and how it changes by year three) evidences documenting roles with an organizational chart (44).

8177-the-global-expansion.why: Part 1 (why the foreign market exists), Part 2 (local currency and the real exchange-rate conversion with its source) and Part 4 (one real problem of going overseas and how to handle it) evidence external factors affecting the industry (74); Part 3 (one specific change to the event or marketing to fit the local culture) evidences external factors shaping the marketing process (80).

8177-secure-the-perimeter.why: Part 1 (where fans go and why) and Part 2 (the map with routes and how the main gate avoids a bottleneck) evidence a venue's security needs such as evacuation, capacity and clear egress (90); the written plan with Part 4 (the three-sentence PA announcement) and Part 5 (a school drill as an EAP) evidences emergency preparedness plans (91), and Part 3 (where police, guest services and trainers go and each group's job) evidences types of security and partner agencies (89).

8177-the-back-room.why: Part 1 (the discrepancy log comparing purchase order, packing slip and count for every item) evidences the controlling function of managing the shop (41); Part 2 (the inventory table of usable items and why the rest can't be used) evidences managing resources (14), and Part 3 (the professional supplier email with PO number and credit amount) evidences job-related technical skills in math and communication (26).

8177-the-battle-for-the-entertainment-do.why: Part 1 (the persona, their week and budget) and Part 2 (their top motivator and why it fits) evidence factors that motivate consumers to attend (93); Part 3 (a specific local indirect competitor and why it is a threat) and Part 4 (a promotion that wins the persona over that competitor) evidence how competitive factors and event attractiveness relate to attendance (94).

8177-the-bottom-line.why: Parts 1 to 3 (projected revenue from fees, tickets and concessions, every expense line, and a budget that reaches a 15% margin) evidence developing an event budget (98); Part 2 (labeling each expense fixed or variable) evidences budget components (85), and Part 3 (net profit and profit margin, revised if under 15%) with Part 4 (the CFO memo on the two biggest risks) evidences analyzing an income statement (88).

8177-the-final-whistle.why: Parts 2 to 6 together (career paths, resume bullets, STAR stories, network and barrier strategies) evidence developing a career plan (108); Part 2 (three jobs with what each involves and which class project prepared you) evidences evaluating career opportunities (43), and Part 2 (the education and training each job requires) evidences education and training needs (104).

8177-the-franchise-evolution.why: Parts 1 to 3 (a priced bundle, a brand extension and a naming-rights deal as three new ways to make money) evidence revenue sources (86); Part 1 (the bundle of tickets, food and extras with savings) and Part 3 (a named stadium area and sponsor fit) evidence on-site revenue streams (46), and Part 4 (the Kickers' life-cycle stage and how the three ideas help them grow) evidences planning from a review of past performance (23).

8177-the-front-lines.why: Part 2 (the T.H.A.N.K.S. service script for the fan behind the pillar) evidences customer service skills (9); Part 1 (the six-step sales script with open-ended questions and three features turned into benefits) evidences responding to customer inquiries (60), and Part 2 (the solution offered and why it is fair to both the fan and the team) evidences explaining company policy to a customer (61).

8177-the-nil-deal.why: Part 1 (choosing the public figure and why their audience beats someone with more followers), Part 2 (macro or micro with one advantage and one risk) and Part 4 (the numbers that show whether the deal worked) evidence the manager's role in campaign decision-making (42); Part 3 (the mockup with a clear #ad or #sponsored FTC disclosure) evidences the effect of national law on the industry (75).

8177-the-sponsorship-negotiation.why: Part 2 (Feel, Felt, Found answers to the two most likely objections) and Part 3 (how the student stayed calm and pivoted after a no) evidence conflict-resolution skills (6); Part 1 (at least two prospects owned by women or minority-group members or serving Richmond's diverse communities) evidences respect for diversity (8), and Part 1 (the CRM tracker built in Google Sheets with a status pipeline) evidences working knowledge of IT systems (17).

8177-the-ticket-office.why: Parts 1, 2 and 4 together (setting quotas, designing a contest and supporting a struggling rep) evidence the planning, leading and controlling functions of a manager (41); Part 1 (plans needed for $60,000 and each rep's quota with the math shown) evidences job-specific math (19), and Part 3 (the three-rule code of ethics and the problem each rule prevents) evidences ethical issues in the industry (63).
